top_categories.workout_context: 10,800ft of climbing makes aerobic ceiling relevant when the grade or pace changes. VO2max work supports those hard moments; sustained climbing and conservative pacing remain the spine.
92ft/mi signals a climbing-heavy course. Sustained sub-threshold and threshold work builds the steady power needed without turning the opening climb into the day’s hardest effort.
At Triple Bypass — Colorado's Three-Pass Challenge, changes in grade or pace can lift effort above threshold before it settles again. Over-unders train that transition while you keep riding.
At mile 60 of 118, glycogen is gone. This workout teaches your body to produce watts on fumes.
Race-pace efforts that mimic Triple Bypass — Colorado's Three-Pass Challenge's demands. Pacing, fueling, and tactical decisions under fatigue. Practice the race before July.
10,800ft of climbing on grades that change every minute. You need to switch from seated to standing without losing rhythm.
88–92% FTP is where you'll spend the hardest sustained miles of Triple Bypass — Colorado's Three-Pass Challenge. Train it until it feels boring.
Every hard session works better with a bigger aerobic base. At 118 miles, base fitness is the difference between racing and surviving.

Road-specific control matters at Triple Bypass — Colorado's Three-Pass Challenge. Practice on paved mountain highways and dedicated bike paths: use smooth gear and cadence changes, accelerate deliberately out of corners, and settle quickly back into sustainable power for 118 miles.
Low-cadence force work supports 10,800ft of climbing when the grade lowers cadence. Practice controlled torque while preserving good form.
Endurance with intensity spikes baked in. Exactly what 10,800ft of climbing on paved mountain highways and dedicated bike paths does to your power file on race day.
118 miles rewards fat oxidation. This volume work shifts your fuel mix so you're still burning fat at hour 5, not bonking at hour 3.

race_overlay.nutrition: Target 60–80g carbs/hour for Triple Bypass — Colorado's Three-Pass Challenge’s 118 miles. Start fueling within the first 30 minutes — early fueling prevents late-race collapse. Bonking at mile 60 is a nutrition failure, not a fitness failure.
race_overlay.altitude: Triple Bypass — Colorado's Three-Pass Challenge includes meaningful altitude exposure. Reduced oxygen availability can affect sustainable power, pacing, and recovery. Use a conservative upper-mountain pacing plan, test any travel or acclimatization strategy before the event, and plan layers for changing conditions. Do not begin iron or other supplements without clinician-guided testing. Temperature range from cool dawn to warm valleys to cold pass summits; High-altitude sun exposure — intense UV above 9,000 ft.

pack_summary: This 10-workout pack focuses on VO2max, TT Threshold, and Over Under to prepare you for 118 miles of paved mountain highways and dedicated bike paths in Evergreen to Avon, Colorado.
